slides.headline: He spent his life reading the story written in stone - fossilized plants that proved India's past stretched back hundreds of millions of years.
Birbal Sahni was born on November 14, 1891.
slides.body: He became India's foremost palaeobotanist, studying fossilized plants to piece together the subcontinent's prehistoric past, and brought a field that barely existed in India into serious scientific standing.

slides.headline: He founded an institute dedicated entirely to that science.
slides.body: In 1946, Sahni established the Institute of Palaeobotany in Lucknow. Today, as the Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences, it remains an autonomous research body under India's Department of Science and Technology - still running, eight decades later.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat still needs scientists willing to build the field, not just work in it.
slides.body: Sahni didn't just study fossils - he built the institution that let India keep studying them, long after he was gone.
